title: Mapping the Legal Gray Zone: When Does AI-Assisted Penetration Testing Become Computer Fraud?

original_idea.body:
# Mapping the Legal Gray Zone: When Does AI-Assisted Penetration Testing Become Computer Fraud?

**Problem:** AI dramatically lowers the barrier to penetration testing, but the legal boundary between authorized pen testing (with AI assistance) and unauthorized access under CFAA and EU NIS2 is ambiguous.

**Direction:** Analyze CFAA, EU NIS2, and UK CMA statutes for how authorization requirements apply to AI-assisted testing. Identify 5 specific AI-assisted actions (automated port scanning, AI-generated exploit code, autonomous vulnerability chaining) and map their legal status under each framework. Identify the governance gaps.

**Why it matters:** Legal ambiguity in AI-assisted security research creates a chilling effect on defensive research and provides attackers with plausible deniability arguments. Mapping the gray zone informs both law reform and governance design.

**Relevant context:** OpenAI Trusted Access legal safe harbor provisions; Linder et al. Expected Legitimate Frequency dimension; CFAA and EU NIS2.
